bottom_line: In RE-DEEM, compared with placebo, dabigatran added to dual antiplatelet therapy increased major or clinically relevant minor bleeding in a dose-dependent manner, with hazard ratios of 1.77 (95% confidence intervals 0.70, 4.50) for 50 mg and 4.27 (1.86, 9.81) for 150 mg.
implications: These data support that adding dabigatran to background antiplatelet therapy increased major or clinically relevant minor bleeding versus placebo (e.g., 2.2% with placebo vs 7.9% with dabigatran 110 mg and 7.8% with 150 mg; HR 3.92 and 4.27, respectively), while ischaemic outcomes were reported descriptively with low event counts and only minor numerical differences (e.g., 3.8% placebo vs 3.0% with 110 mg).

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-escalation trial in post-MI patients largely on dual antiplatelet therapy.
major_points.quote: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-escalation trial, 1861 patients (99.2% on dual antiplatelet treatment)

major_points.text: Patients were randomized to dabigatran 50, 75, 110, or 150 mg twice daily, or placebo.
major_points.quote: randomized to twice daily treatment with dabigatran 50 mg (n ¼ 369), 75 mg (n ¼ 368), 110 mg (n ¼ 406), 150 mg (n ¼ 347), or placebo (n ¼ 371).

major_points.text: Primary outcome was composite of major or clinically relevant minor bleeding during the 6-month treatment period.
major_points.quote: Primary outcome was the composite of major or clinically rel- evant minor bleeding during the 6-month treatment period.

major_points.text: Dose-dependent increase in primary bleeding outcome versus placebo, with HRs reported for each dabigatran dose.
major_points.quote: dose-dependent increase with dabigatran, hazard ratio (HR) 1.77 (95% confidence intervals 0.70, 4.50) for 50 mg; HR 2.17 (0.88, 5.31) for 75 mg; HR 3.92 (1.72, 8.95) for 110 mg; and HR 4.27 (1.86, 9.81) for 150 mg.

major_points.text: D-dimer concentrations were reduced in all dabigatran dose groups versus placebo at weeks 1 and 4.
major_points.quote: Compared with placebo, D-dimer concentrations were reduced in all dabigatran dose groups by an average of 37 and 45% at weeks 1 and 4, respectively (P , 0.001).

major_points.text: Composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal MI, or non-haemorrhagic stroke was numerically similar across groups (descriptive).

absolute_effects.text: Primary outcome (major or clinically relevant minor bleeding): placebo 8 (2.2) vs dabigatran 110 mg 32 (7.9).
Major bleeding (ISTH definition): placebo 2 (0.5) vs dabigatran 150 mg 4 (1.2).
Composite cardiovascular death, non-fatal MI, or non-haemorrhagic stroke: placebo 14 (3.8) vs dabigatran 110 mg 12 (3.0).
All-cause death: placebo 14 (3.8) vs dabigatran 50 mg 8 (2.2).
